title: Cookie policy
excerpt: Every cookie and every storage key this site uses, with names, purposes and lifetimes — and what is deliberately absent.
meta_title: Cookie policy — the one cookie Onim sets, and when
meta_description: Every cookie and storage key used on Onim, with names and lifetimes, plus what the site deliberately does not set and how to clear it.
content:
This page lists every cookie and every piece of browser storage Onim uses, what each one is for, and how long it lasts. There are very few of them. There are no advertising cookies on the site as shipped, no third-party tracking scripts, and no consent wall, because there is nothing to consent to in order to use a calculator.

What a cookie is, in one paragraph

A cookie is a small text file a website asks your browser to keep on your device and to send back with each later request to that site. It cannot read other files, it cannot run a program, and it cannot see other websites' cookies. Browsers also offer two other kinds of storage — local storage and session storage — which hold small values on your device without sending them to the server on every request. Onim uses one cookie and one local-storage key, both described below.

The cookie the public site sets

First-party cookies
NameWhat it holdsWhyLifetime
onim_vid A random 24-character hexadecimal token, for example 9f2c1a…. It contains no name, email address or location. It is created the first time you like a calculator or post a review, and it is read afterwards only to stop the same browser from registering the same like twice. It is also what makes "you have already liked this calculator" possible. Up to 12 months, then it expires. Clearing site data resets it immediately.

onim_vid is a first-party cookie: it is set by this site for this site. It is marked HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it, and SameSite=Lax, so it is not sent when another website links you here from a form. It is not used for advertising, not used to build a profile, and not shared with anyone.

Local storage on your device

Browser storage
KeyWhat it holdsWhyLifetime
omni_preferred The single value yes or no. Remembers whether you pressed "Add as preferred on Google" on this device, so the button shows the right state when you return. It never leaves your browser and is never sent to us. Until you clear site data, or press the button again.

Local storage stays on your device. Unlike a cookie it is not attached to your requests, so the server never sees it.

The admin area's session cookie

The site's administration panel — a separate area at /admin, not part of the public site — uses one PHP session cookie called onim_sid to keep an editor signed in. It is set only after a successful login, it is HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, and it is destroyed when the editor signs out. A visitor to any public page never receives it.

What is not here

  • No analytics cookies on the site as shipped. Page counts come from the server's own counter, not from a script in your browser.
  • No advertising cookies on the site as shipped. The ad placements in the page are empty until an operator fills them.
  • No social media pixels, no heat-mapping scripts, no A/B testing framework, no tag manager.
  • No cookie banner, because the one cookie above is strictly functional: it exists only because you used a feature that requires it.

If the operator enables analytics

A deployment can switch on one analytics provider in the admin panel. When one is active, its script loads on every page and sets its own cookies under its own terms; this site does not merge that data with anything else. The providers that can be selected are:

  • Plausible — cookieless by design. It records page views without a persistent identifier.
  • Umami — cookieless by default, recording aggregate page views and referrers.
  • Google Analytics 4 — sets first-party cookies (_ga and _ga_*, up to 13 months) and processes data under Google's terms. If it is switched on here, those cookies appear in your browser and can be blocked or deleted in the usual way.

The current state of this deployment is stated in the answer below, so you do not have to take a general statement on trust.

If the operator enables advertising

The site has ad placements in fixed positions — never inside a calculation, never between a question and its answer. When a placement is filled by a third-party network, that network may set cookies for frequency capping, fraud prevention and measurement, and may use them across the sites it serves. Those cookies are set by the network, not by Onim, and they fall under that network's policy; the placement itself is labelled as advertising wherever it appears. As shipped, no network script is loaded and no such cookie is set.

Controlling cookies on your side

Every major browser lets you see, block and delete cookies and site data. Blocking onim_vid breaks nothing except the memory of which pages you have already liked — the site works normally without it. Blocking local storage likewise only affects the preferred-source button. If you never press a like button or post a review, no cookie is set on your device at all.

Most browsers also offer a private or incognito window, which discards all of this when you close it. The file tools work there too, because they never needed a server in the first place.

The current configuration of this deployment

  • Analytics: none — no third-party analytics script is loaded.
  • Advertising: no network tags are loaded; ad placements are empty.
  • Cookies set on a normal visit: none. onim_vid appears only after you like a calculator or post a review.

Questions

If something in your browser's cookie list looks like it came from this site and is not described here, send the name through the contact form and it will be traced and either explained or removed. The privacy policy covers the wider question of what the site does with data, and your data and your choices explains how to have anything removed.
